# Municipal Ordinance No. 001, Series of 2006

**An Ordinance Creating the Municipal Water and Sanitation Development Council (Municipal WATSAN) of the Local Government Unit of Pitogo, Quezon**

## Summary

This ordinance creates the Municipal Water and Sanitation Development Council (Municipal WATSAN) for the [[Municipality of Pitogo]]. The council is tasked with designing and implementing a long-term water supply and sanitation plan aimed at achieving 100% sustainable access to safe water and adequate basic sanitation. The ordinance establishes the council's composition, functions, and mandate to coordinate all water and sanitation projects across the municipality's barangays.

## Key Provisions

**Section 1 — Short Title.** The ordinance shall be known as the ordinance creating the Municipal Water and Development Council (Municipal WATSAN).

**Section 2 — Role of Municipal Local Government Units.** The municipal LGU is one of the two main partners of the program. It is the custodian of grant money channeled from DPWH, which delegates disbursement to the Municipal WATSAN Development Council as the project implementing arm. The roles of the Municipal LGU include: (1) assign counterpart staff to the project; (2) set the local counterpart contribution to total project cost based on feedback from the Barangay Assembly; (3) provide counterpart contribution in support of the project; (4) provide technical and institutional assistance to participating barangays; and (5) monitor and generate feedback on the implementation of projects.

**Section 3 — Roles of Municipal Water and Sanitation Development Council.** The council shall perform the task of designing and implementing a long-term water supply and sanitation program aimed at achieving 100% sustainable access to safe and adequate sanitation. Specific functions include:
- (a) Design a long-term water supply and sanitation plan for the municipality
- (b) Oversee the implementation of the plan
- (c) Coordinate all project activities related to water supply and sanitation across different barangays
- (d) Review and recommend policy changes in the implementation of water supply and sanitation projects to the Municipal Development Council
- (e) Recommend measures and safeguards against pollution and for the preservation of the natural ecosystem
- (f) Recommend measures to generate resources, funding, and implementation of projects as specified in the duly approved Municipal Water Supply and Sanitation Plan
- (g) Identify areas in the municipality with common water and sanitation problems as basis for planning local water supply and sanitation systems
- (h) See to it that the required water permits and Certificates of Public Conveyance (CPC) are secured from the NWRB for all water systems within its domain
- (i) Facilitate the clustering of barangays to solve common water supply and sanitation problems
- (j) Prioritize implementation of water supply and sanitation projects among barangays in the context of limited and scarce resources
- (k) Spearhead an educational campaign to promote sustainable and ecologically friendly approaches in implementing water supply and sanitation projects
- (l) Convene regular meetings for the Municipal WATSAN Development Council at least every month for purposes of integrating, synchronizing, monitoring, and evaluating the development and implementation of the plan and its projects
- (m) Spearhead social and institutional programs to ensure system sustainability

**Section 4 — Composition.** The Council is chaired by the Municipal Mayor or his designated representative, with the following as permanent members:
- A. Municipal Planning and Development Coordinator
- B. Municipal Treasurer
- C. Municipal Health Officer
- D. Municipal Environment and Natural Resources Officer
- E. Municipal Engineer
- F. Municipal Social Welfare and Development Officer
- G. Water District General Manager
- H. SB Member — Chairman of Committee on Public Works

The Council shall also include three non-government representatives from: (A) NGOs or POs whose principal purpose is provision of community-based water supply and sanitation systems; (B) existing community-based water and sanitation organizations; (C) academic sector specialists in water sanitation engineering, public health, hydro-geology, public administration, business management, and community development.

**Section 5 — Repealing Clause.** Any ordinance or part thereof inconsistent with this ordinance is hereby repealed.

**Section 6 — Effectivity.** The ordinance shall take effect immediately upon its approval.
